what.text: Refugees who were displaced from Afghanistan live in host countries including Pakistan, Iran, Germany, France, and United Kingdom.
At the end of 2025, Pakistan hosted 1158538 refugees from Afghanistan.
In the same year, Iran hosted 758339 refugees from Afghanistan.

why.text: Causes include the Armed conflict over the government of Afghanistan active from 1978 to 2025, involving groups such as PDPA, Taleban, NRF, and AFF.

Fighting also involved the Armed conflict with the Islamic State group, Afghanistan active from 2015 to 2025 against IS, and the Interstate armed conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan active from 2024 to 2025 against Government of Pakistan.
Key events during these periods include the Soviet intervention in 1979 when Soviet forces entered Afghanistan, and the Taliban taking control of Kabul in 2021.

when.text: Refugees from Afghanistan in Iran and Pakistan combined numbered 500000 in 1979 and reached 6314110 in 1990.

After Soviet forces entered Afghanistan in 1979, refugee figures in Iran and Pakistan rose steeply from 1980, while in 2002 returns from Pakistan and Iran were the largest in UNHCR data following the fall of the Taliban government.
New arrivals in Iran and Pakistan followed when the Taliban took control of Kabul in 2021, and large returns of Afghans followed after Pakistan announced a repatriation plan in 2023.

how.text: The sources don't say what travel routes people used or details of their living conditions.
Refugee figures for Iran and Pakistan represent year-end totals for those two host countries combined, rather than a complete total for all host countries.

Internal displacement inside Afghanistan is measured separately through year-end totals of conflict-displaced people whom UNHCR protects or assists, alongside internal displacement estimates recorded by IDMC.
